models_evaluated: In-house DeepLab V3 automatic contouring system (first generation)
In-house nnU-Net V2 automatic contouring system (second generation)

links.outcome: Local contour agreement and failure rate after model update
links.effect: After update, mean DSC improved from 0.88 to 0.93 for CTV and 0.88 to 0.95 for OARs (P < 0.001); mean failure rate decreased from 3.30% to 0.64%.
links.quote: Therefore, after iterative updating, the similarities between the automatic results and the AI‐assisted final contours in the post‐update cohort were superior to those in the post‐implementation cohort.

openai.sample_unit: patients (150 longitudinal-cohort patients and 21 independent performance-evaluation patients)

links.effect: Final contours, pooling manual and AI-assisted methods: 99.2% (125/126) scored ≥ 4. Unedited contours scored ≥ 4 in 28.6% (6/21) for Auto1 and 95.2% (20/21) for Auto2.
links.quote: First, among the 126 final contours produced by the six participating oncologists, 99.2% (125/126) received a Likert score of ≥ 4, with only one contour rated 3.5, indicating that nearly all final contours produced by the six oncologists required only minor or no further edits.

links.outcome: Contouring failures associated with variation in patient positioning
links.effect: Supine rather than prone positioning was identified as a failure mode affecting CTV prediction; position-specific failure rates were not reported.
links.quote: However, older or physically weak patients who cannot maintain this position may be scanned supine, thereby introducing variability that affected CTV prediction.

links.outcome: Local automatic-contouring failure rate after model update
links.effect: Mean failure rate decreased from 3.30% to 0.64% after updating from Auto1 to Auto2, rather than showing post-update deterioration.
links.quote: After automatic contouring system update, the mean failure rate decreased from 3.30% to 0.64%.

unlisted_practices: Evaluating real-world AI editing burden by comparing unedited AI outputs against final clinically approved outputs
Conducting longitudinal evaluations across pre-implementation, post-implementation, and post-update phases to assess AI impact on clinical workflows
Systematically analyzing AI failure modes and root causes jointly with clinical and technical experts
Measuring inter-observer consistency, accuracy, and efficiency of human-AI collaboration compared to manual baselines

screen.practice: post-deployment model update with quality assurance and clinician editing of auto-contours
screen.reason: The study evaluates the longitudinal real-world clinical impact of implementing and iteratively updating an automated radiotherapy contouring system, directly comparing clinical outcomes, failure rates, and efficiency across pre-implementation, post-implementation, and post-update phases.
